plan.component: 1. Gap assessment and follow-up asking (preflight + decide_followup)
plan.what_it_does: Verified in code. (1) advance_case (backend/app/analysis/pipeline.py:63-84) calls assess_gaps (pipeline.py:87-99), which calls assess_case (backend/app/analysis/assess.py:13-30). That function is one request_stage call with system=case_assessment_prompt() and content={response_language, case_sources, followup_history}, and its output is validated against CaseAssessmentTrace. No temperature is passed, so the provider's default sampling applies (backend/app/llm/request.py:256-257 sets temperature only when one is given). (2) The prompt (backend/app/analysis/prompts.py:271-288) is triage only: no claims, and affected_claim_ids is always empty (prompts.py:283). It embeds GAP_IDENTIFICATION_INSTRUCTIONS (prompts.py:18-42), which checks the case against CASE_CHECKLIST (prompts.py:5-14: who_affected, who_responsible, what, when, where, why, how, how_much). A materially unanswered, ambiguous or conflicting item becomes a gap whose gap_key is that key (prompts.py:22-24). The statuses are NOT_PROVIDED, EXPLICITLY_UNKNOWN, AMBIGUOUS and CONFLICTING (prompts.py:34). EXPLICITLY_UNKNOWN is askable=false (prompts.py:35). Each askable high-priority gap gets one question of at most 300 characters (prompts.py:37-39). (3) The schema: CaseAnalysisGap (backend/app/trace/claims.py:214-246) has gap_key, topic, status Literal (claims.py:220), priority high/medium/low (224), askable (225) and clarification_question (226-228); a question over 300 characters is silently set to None (240-246). CaseAssessmentTrace holds at most 32 gaps (claims.py:249-253). The gap has no field for the text that answers or fails to answer a key, so its status cannot be checked by code today. (4) The policy: decide_followup (backend/app/followup/clarification.py:44-65) proceeds when rounds_spent > max_rounds (53) or the round budget is spent (55). Otherwise it asks candidates[0] (58-60), the first gap in the model's output order that is priority=="high", askable, has a question and has a key not yet asked (eligible_gaps, clarification.py:30-41). The model's listing order is therefore the ranking. The defaults are 3 rounds of 3 questions (backend/app/config.py:79-80; pipeline.py:39-41), and rounds_spent is 1-based (backend/app/analysis/run.py:147). A round that asks returns before the MITRE gate or RAG runs (pipeline.py:73-74). (5) answerable_gap (backend/app/trace/bind.py:105-111) applies only to the final trace, not to preflight gaps. The binder's quote locator located_quote (bind.py:232-236) is what a B1 harness would reuse. (6) The research harness replays round 1 through production decide_followup (research/casie_clarification/detect.py:86-97). The same-budget baseline uses the fixed order who_affected, who_responsible, when, what, how_much, how, where (detect.py:29; robustness.py:23, 64).
evaluation_questions: Q1 (causal). Does the preflight ask about a checklist key because its fact is missing from the text? Test: the paired withholding test, the same key on the visible text against the full text.

Q2 (targeting). At the same question budget, are the system's round-1 questions better aimed at missing facts than a checklist that has not read the case? The checklist is scored order-free (the expectation over random orders and the distribution over all 5,040 orders), not only in the one frozen order.
Q3 (status). When the preflight flags a key, is the status right? NOT_PROVIDED should mean the text states no fact of that key; AMBIGUOUS should mean a fact is stated but vaguely.
Q4 (ranking). Do priority and listing order carry information about missingness? That is, does decide_followup's choice of candidates[0] among high-priority gaps add anything over listing?

Q5 (fix B1). If the preflight must quote the text that answers each key, and code checks the quote, does absence become the cause of asking (Q1 turns positive)? Does the status become correct (Q3)? How much of the change comes from code verification, as against the model's own claim that it has a quote?
Q6 (why). Can the 'why' key be evaluated on CASIE at all, and with what power?

Q7 (optional, paid). How much of the visible-against-full discordance is run-to-run sampling noise? When a reader declines, does the next preflight mark the key EXPLICITLY_UNKNOWN and keep the same key?

problems.problem: P1. Asking is not caused by missingness: the preflight flags a key about as often when its fact is present as when it was withheld.
problems.evidence: McNemar p ranges from 0.296 to 1.000 across all label variants (robustness.md). On the full article, where nothing is withheld, 90 of 100 cases still ask at least one round-1 question: 184 questions on full against 207 on visible (computed here from the jsonl). The share of listed high-priority askable NOT_PROVIDED gaps is 181 on full against 195 on visible.

problems.problem: P2. The status is uninformative: NOT_PROVIDED is used for facts the text states. Missing and vague are not separated.
problems.evidence: Computed here, presence labels (CASIE argument present in the text = negative or mixed; ours: absent counts as missing). Of keys asked on the visible text whose fact is present, 57 of 69 (0.83) are NOT_PROVIDED; on the full text, 90 of 101 (0.89). For keys asked whose fact is missing, 123 of 134 (0.92) are NOT_PROVIDED. So the status barely shifts between present and missing. Frozen FPs: 28 of 34 NOT_PROVIDED.

problems.problem: P3. Priority, which decide_followup filters on (clarification.py:37), does not separate missing from present keys.
problems.evidence: Computed here, visible text, listed gaps on checklist keys: high priority for 41 of 56 (0.73) positive keys and 44 of 57 (0.77) negative keys.

problems.problem: P4. Recall is capped by the round budget and by the model's listing order, because candidates[0] is taken in output order (clarification.py:58-60).
problems.evidence: Listed R 0.56 against asked R 0.42 (README.md:281-282). Pilot case 10374: the withheld key 'how' was listed but not asked (README.md:246-248). Gap order follows checklist order in only 46 of 100 visible runs (computed here).

problems.problem: P5. The frozen fixed-order baseline is order-dependent on the four same-named keys, and the frozen order favours the baseline's recall there. The 'recall reverses on four keys' reading is an artefact of the order.
problems.evidence: Computed here over all 5,040 orders at the system's per-run budget (0 questions in 10 runs, 1 in 13, 2 in 41, 3 in 36). Seven keys: the system (P 0.541, R 0.417) beats every order; the best order reaches P 0.535 and R 0.385. Random-order expectation: P 0.412, R 0.292. Four keys: 19.0% of orders reach the system's precision and 21.0% its recall. Random-order expectation P 0.392, R 0.299 against the system's 0.490/0.436. The frozen order gives 0.31/0.53.

problems.problem: P6. who_responsible gold is noisy (CASIE Attacker includes nominals and victims), which inflates FPs on that key.
problems.evidence: README.md:295-300, 369-374; A2a leaves who_responsible absent in 95 of 100 cases.

problems.problem: P7. Run-to-run sampling noise is unknown. No temperature is set (assess.py:20-30; request.py:256-257), and one run per text means part of the b and c discordance in the McNemar test could be noise.
problems.evidence: No repeated main-run preflight exists; the pilot's 3 runs covered only 3 cases.

problems.problem: P8. 'why' is outside the frozen evaluation and is rarely asked.
problems.evidence: Purpose was excluded (README.md:24, 197). Computed here: 'why' was asked in round 1 in 4 of 100 visible runs and 0 of 100 full runs; 37 why gaps were listed across 200 runs. Placing CASIE Purpose arguments by offset (ours) gives 10 positive, 14 negative, 12 mixed and 64 absent cases, too few for inference.

problems.problem: P9. Multi-round behaviour is untested at scale: EXPLICITLY_UNKNOWN after a declined answer, and key drift that would re-ask the same fact under another key. Code blocks re-asking only by gap_key (clarification.py:40).
problems.evidence: Only 5 dry-run cases (README.md:181-182); the recovery arms were set aside (README.md:189-195).

baselines.name: Ask nothing
baselines.description: Predicts no key (recall 0).
baselines.why_fair: It is the lower bound, with the same labels and cases (robustness.py:62).

baselines.name: Checklist, all
baselines.description: Predicts every key: recall 1, precision equal to the prevalence.
baselines.why_fair: It is the upper bound on recall. Its precision equals the base rate (0.41 on seven keys), which shows what reading the case adds.

baselines.name: Checklist, same budget, frozen order
baselines.description: The first n keys of who_affected, who_responsible, when, what, how_much, how, where, with n = the system's asked count in that run.
baselines.why_fair: The budget is matched, but the result depends on the order: three of the four same-named keys come first. Keep it only as the pre-registered comparison.

baselines.name: Checklist, same budget, random order (expected) and all-orders distribution
baselines.description: The same n per run, averaged exactly over all 5,040 orders. Report the system's percentile among the orders and the best order found post hoc as a ceiling.
baselines.why_fair: It removes the order choice, which was ours. Its precision equals the prevalence, so it is the correct chance baseline for 'asking without reading'. It is free, and the numbers are already computed here (P5).

baselines.name: Production preflight on the full text (withholding control)
baselines.description: The same call on the article with nothing withheld.
baselines.why_fair: It is a paired, within-case control: the only change is the presence of the withheld sentences. This is the MediQ and ERASER-style perturbation.

baselines.name: B1-selfreport (ablation)
baselines.description: The same B1 outputs, but a key counts as present whenever the model supplies any quote, with no code check.
baselines.why_fair: The call and the outputs are identical and only the decision rule differs. It isolates the contribution of code verification at zero extra cost.

datasets.name: CASIE (100 main cases of research/casie_clarification, seeded order)
datasets.citation: Satyapanich, Ferraro and Finin. CASIE: Extracting Cybersecurity Event Information from Text. AAAI 2020 (local F:/CASIE; no licence stated, evaluation only, never redistributed: README.md:14-17)
datasets.labels_used: Author labels: Attack events of subtypes Databreach, Phishing and Ransom; argument roles with character offsets (cases.py:55-62); for the 'why' analysis only, Purpose arguments by offset.
datasets.our_rules: OURS, all fixed before computing: (a) the withholding rule, 2 non-lead sentences with the most distinct facts (cases.py:66-68); (b) the 12 scored roles and whole-token matching after normalisation (cases.py:26-31, 46-48); (c) the key to role mapping (README.md:156-167). Four keys are same-named and one-to-one (who_affected→Victim, who_responsible→Attacker, when→Time, where→Place) and are primary for B1 as the README pre-registers (README.md:381-384). what, how and how_much need interpretation and are secondary. (d) The positive/negative/mixed/absent label rule (README.md:202-207). (e) The presence-variant label proposed here: a fact present = negative or mixed; missing = positive or absent. absent assumes CASIE annotation is complete, which is a known risk. (f) A2a and A2b named-mention rules (README.md:322-330). (g) Purpose placement by sentence offset for 'why'. (h) For B1 AMBIGUOUS scoring only: a vague mention is a nominal Attacker or Victim (A2b capitalisation rule) or a Time argument with no digit or month name. Each rule is pre-registered with a free sensitivity check (four keys against seven; frozen against presence; A2a against A2b).

datasets.name: AnnoCTR (optional out-of-domain check; not core)
datasets.citation: AnnoCTR, LREC-COLING 2024 (local F:/anno-ctr-lrec-coling-2024/AnnoCTR): 120 CTI reports; ne_tags ORG 1,578, LOC 1,155, SECTOR 552; TimeML TIMEX3 files (counted here). The exact reference is to be taken from the verified RQ1 tables before use.
datasets.labels_used: Author labels: TIMEX3 temporal expressions and LOC entities.
datasets.our_rules: OURS: TIMEX3→when and LOC→where, the same withholding rule. ORG has no actor or victim role, so who_* keys cannot be labelled. CTI reports are not incident narratives and carry a creation date (DCT), so 'when' is almost always present. Listed as a limit, not planned as a paid run.

metrics.name: Detection precision, recall, F1 (pooled and per key)
metrics.definition: A key is predicted if it is asked in round 1 (primary) or listed (secondary). The gold is positive or negative by the frozen rule; mixed and absent are excluded.
metrics.precedent: Chaparro et al., Detecting Missing Information in Bug Descriptions, ESEC/FSE 2017, doi:10.1145/3106237.3106285 (verified in related_studies_modules.md). F2 is OUR weighting, not InsufficiencyBench's (README.md:376-379).

metrics.name: Withholding flip test (primary causal metric)
metrics.definition: For each withheld (positive) key: b = flagged on the visible text only, c = flagged on the full text only. Exact two-sided McNemar test, with a case-level bootstrap of the difference in rates beside it.
metrics.precedent: Perturbation or withholding: MediQ (NeurIPS 2024, doi:10.52202/079017-0908); Wen, Howe and Wang, Findings EMNLP 2024, doi:10.18653/v1/2024.findings-emnlp.197; ERASER, ACL 2020 (2020.acl-main.408). McNemar: Dietterich, Neural Computation 10(7), 1998, doi:10.1162/089976698300017197 (checked on Crossref in this pass).

metrics.name: NOT_PROVIDED-on-present rate (status error)
metrics.definition: Among flagged keys whose fact the text states (CASIE argument present), the share with status NOT_PROVIDED. Report it beside P(NOT_PROVIDED | missing), so the status's discrimination is visible. The current value is 0.83 against 0.92 (P2).
metrics.precedent: Scoring answerable and unanswerable cases separately: Rajpurkar, Jia and Liang, SQuAD 2.0, ACL 2018, doi:10.18653/v1/P18-2124 (checked on Crossref). Sufficient against insufficient context: Joren et al., ICLR 2025 (verified, research_moves_2026-09-29.md).

metrics.name: Quote bind rate and support precision (B1)
metrics.definition: Bind rate: the share of model-supplied per-key quotes that located_quote finds in the visible text. Support precision: the share of bound quotes whose span overlaps a CASIE argument of that key's roles, by offsets. The gold is the author labels plus our key-role mapping; the four keys are primary.
metrics.precedent: Citation precision in ALCE (Gao et al., EMNLP 2023, doi:10.18653/v1/2023.emnlp-main.398) and Attribute First, then Generate (Slobodkin et al., ACL 2024, doi:10.18653/v1/2024.acl-long.182), both verified in related_studies_modules.md. CyberCase checks only verbatim occurrence, not entailment.

metrics.name: Self-report gap (B1 against B1-selfreport)
metrics.definition: The difference in detection P/R, withholding b−c and NOT_PROVIDED-on-present rate between a decision rule that trusts any model quote and one that trusts only bound quotes. Also report the count of 'hallucinated presence': a quote given but not bound.
metrics.precedent: Motivation for external rather than self verification: Huang et al., Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet, ICLR 2024 per the arXiv comment, arXiv:2310.01798 (checked on arXiv in this pass).

metrics.name: Order-free same-budget baseline
metrics.definition: The exact expectation over all 7! checklist orders of TP, FP and FN at the system's per-run n, plus the system's percentile among the orders.
metrics.precedent: Evaluation under a fixed question budget: Zhang and Choi, Clarify When Necessary, Findings NAACL 2025, doi:10.18653/v1/2025.findings-naacl.306 (verified). Averaging over orders is OUR construction.

metrics.name: Paired randomization test with Holm correction; BCa and percentile intervals; MDE
metrics.definition: Arms are swapped within a case, 10,000 times, seed fixed. A case-level bootstrap of 2,000 resamples.
metrics.precedent: Dror et al., ACL 2018, doi:10.18653/v1/P18-1128; Bowyer et al., ICML 2025, PMLR v267; Card et al., EMNLP 2020, doi:10.18653/v1/2020.emnlp-main.745 (all verified in research_moves_2026-09-29.md).

metrics.name: Test-retest flip rate (optional)
metrics.definition: For each positive key, the share whose asked decision differs between two runs on the same visible text. Compared with the visible-against-full flip rate (b+c)/n.
metrics.precedent: Non-determinism of hosted LLM settings: Atıl et al., Eval4NLP 2025, doi:10.18653/v1/2025.eval4nlp-1.12 (verified).

fixes.fix: B1: a quote-gated preflight. For every checklist key the model returns the exact text that answers it, or null. Code binds the quote (located_quote, bind.py:232-236). A key becomes a gap only when no quote binds (NOT_PROVIDED); a bound quote the model flags as vague gives AMBIGUOUS. decide_followup is unchanged.
fixes.targets_problem: P1 (asking not caused by missingness), P2 (NOT_PROVIDED on stated facts), and the who_responsible 'which group' questions (P6), which become AMBIGUOUS with a bound nominal quote.
fixes.mechanism: Absence is made the cause of asking by construction. A key present in the text yields a bindable quote and cannot be NOT_PROVIDED, so the status is set by a code check rather than the model's judgement.
fixes.literature: Ask-before-Plan (Zhang et al., Findings EMNLP 2024, doi:10.18653/v1/2024.findings-emnlp.636); Majumder et al., NAACL 2021, doi:10.18653/v1/2021.naacl-main.340 (missing = global schema minus local); Joren et al., Sufficient Context, ICLR 2025 (OpenReview); Du and Cardie, EMNLP 2020, doi:10.18653/v1/2020.emnlp-main.49 (role as question). All verified in research_moves_2026-09-29.md.
fixes.how_measured: The B1 main run. Primary, four keys: McNemar b against c (expect b >> c) and P/R against the order-free same-budget baseline. Secondary: the NOT_PROVIDED-on-present rate (current 0.83 visible), support precision, and seven keys plus the presence variant.

fixes.fix: Code verification of the quote, against the model's self-report (the ablation inside B1).

risks_and_limits: The B1 prompt and schema differ from production. A positive B1 result supports a proposed change, not the shipped preflight; adoption needs the owner's approval, and the shipped claim stays 'precision at a fixed budget'.

The key-to-role mapping is ours. The four same-named keys are primary (README.md:381-384); what, how and how_much are interpretive and secondary. The presence variant treats CASIE 'absent' as missing, which assumes complete annotation. CASIE annotates arguments only of annotated events, so a date or place outside an Attack event counts as absent.
The who_responsible gold is unreliable in both directions (README.md:369-374). Report the four keys with and without who_responsible.
Power: 55 positive keys on the four keys; the current MDE for precision is 0.148 (robustness.md). B1 needs a large effect on the McNemar test (b >> c) to be conclusive; one run per case.

B1's cost estimate assumes about 580 extra answer tokens. The upper bound assumes doubled thinking; the harness's per-call reservation enforces the cap.
The B1-selfreport ablation shares outputs with B1. It cannot show whether the instruction 'your quotes will be checked' changes behaviour.
'why' cannot be evaluated inferentially on CASIE (10 positives); Purpose spans are phrases, so only presence is scored, never content.
Everything is measured on English news. Nothing transfers to Thai cases, and the Thai 100-case set stays out; usability (RQ3) is not used.
LADDER and MalwareTextDB have no 5W1H roles. AnnoCTR covers only when and where, with an interpretive mapping and CTI-report dates, so the component has one citable corpus.

fairness_problems: B1's withholding test is partly positive by construction. On the full text the withheld sentence is present, so B1 only has to quote it for the key to count as present and not be asked. 'b >> c' therefore mostly shows that the model can find an answering span. It does not show that asking tracks missingness in a non-trivial way. Frame the B1 McNemar test as a mechanism check. The primary evidence should be detection P/R against the order-free baseline at B1's own budget, plus the false-presence rate: a bound quote on a positive key that does not overlap the key's CASIE roles, which suppresses a needed question.

B1's binding is easy to satisfy. located_quote accepts any exact occurrence up to MAX_QUOTE_CHARS = 2,000 (bind.py:232-236, quotes.py:8). A one-word quote ('hackers', 'today') or a whole paragraph binds, and a long quote overlaps some CASIE argument by chance. Pre-register a quote-length sensitivity: min 2 tokens, max one sentence. Measure support at token level: the share of quote tokens inside an argument of the key's roles, not any overlap.

B1 changes three things at once: a per-key enumeration schema, status definitions, and code gating. The B1-selfreport ablation isolates only the code gate. A gain may come from simply defining the statuses, which the production prompt never does (prompts.py:34). Add the optional definitions-only arm (USD 0.285) or state the confound explicitly.

B1 and production will ask different numbers of questions. Comparing their raw P/R confounds targeting with budget. Compare each against its own-budget order-free baseline, report asks per case, and report the paired case-key McNemar between arms, not unpaired rates.

The only same-budget baselines are case-blind: a checklist in a fixed or random order. A reviewer will call beating a baseline that does not read the case a low bar. Add a free, judge-free baseline that reads the case (ours, pre-registered): a regex for when (a digit year or month name), how_much (a digit plus a unit word) and who_responsible (an ATT&CK group or alias name, the A2a list). It asks a key only when no match occurs in the visible text, with the same per-run budget.

The noise floor comes from a production retest only. B1 would be run once, with no sampling-noise estimate of its own. Its within-arm McNemar discordance cannot be split into noise and effect either. State this, or give the retest budget to a B1 retest if B1 becomes the headline.

Support precision is scored against CASIE annotations. CASIE annotates arguments only of annotated events, so a correct quote of an unannotated date or place counts as unsupported. Report it as 'overlap with annotated argument', a lower bound, not precision.

The best order found post hoc (P 0.535 on seven keys, 0.75 on four) is an oracle chosen on the test data. Present it only as a descriptive ceiling, never as a baseline the system is claimed to beat or lose to.

Harness budget arithmetic that includes the in-flight reservation (8 × about USD 0.0124). Caps: smoke 0.10, B1 main 0.70, retest 0.35, declined 0.25, definitions-only 0.40.

plan.what_it_does: Checked against the code. gate.py:21-28 picks the gate from MITRE_GATE_MODE: 'never' always returns SKIP (gate.py:22), 'encoder' uses the XLM-R gate (gate.py:24), and the default is the LLM gate. The LLM gate (gate_llm.py) makes one request_stage call per case (gate_llm.py:211-218), with temperature 0.0 (gate_llm.py:217) and AnalysisPipelineConfig(output_tokens=1,024) (gate_llm.py:26, 212). The config keeps the default thinking_tokens=8,192 (llm/settings.py:26), so the call goes out with max_tokens = 1,024 + 8,192 = 9,216 (settings.py:31-32) and thinking {type: enabled, budget_tokens: 8192} (llm/request.py:225, 239). The system prompt (gate_llm.py:29-81) asks for RETRIEVE only on 'explicit behavior' (gate_llm.py:36), treats technology as an object as SKIP (gate_llm.py:42), and says 'Optimize precision over recall. IF UNCERTAIN, RETURN SKIP.' (gate_llm.py:52). It has 10 fixed examples, 8 of them Thai (gate_llm.py:58-78). Input: each source is cut to min(4,000, 20,000/number of sources) characters (gate_llm.py:24-25, 84-88, 104), and input_truncated records whether anything was cut (gate_llm.py:91-93, 251). Output is validated by code (gate_llm.py:166-205). Schema failure gives SKIP with invalid_output (:173). RETRIEVE without ids or triggers, an unknown id, a trigger that is not an NFKC substring of a cited source, or a cited source holding no trigger gives SKIP with invalid_grounding (:179, 184, 195, 199). Any provider error fails closed to SKIP with a failure code (:235-251). In retrieve.py a failure_code becomes status 'failed', not 'not_applicable' (retrieve.py:112-113), so the two can be told apart afterwards. The RAG query is the triggers joined by newlines; it falls back to the whole bundle only when there are no triggers, then appends answered follow-ups (retrieve.py:35-50). The encoder gate splits every source in full with PyThaiNLP crfcut, lines first, joining fragments under 25 characters (sentences.py:10, 23, 43). It scores each sentence and RETRIEVEs if any score is at or above the gate.json threshold (gate_encoder.py:82-89), up to 16 triggers of at most 500 characters (gate_encoder.py:22-23, 97-100). The shipped card backend/xlmr_ladder_best/xlmr_ladder_best/gate.json has threshold 0.1, and its only recorded evaluation is the hand-written 46-sentence set. The shadow runs only when mode=llm and shadow=encoder (gate.py:36). It runs concurrently with the LLM gate (retrieve.py:89) and is on only in docker-compose (docker-compose.yml:41, 54); the code default is off (app/config.py:77). Production model: google/gemma-4-26b-a4b-it with providers nextbit/bf16,coreweave/bf16 (docker-compose.yml:39-40). The gate has never run on Gemma in any saved experiment: the analysis baseline ran with the gate off (research/analysis_baseline/run.py:6), and RQ2 ran with MITRE_GATE_MODE=never (research/report_fidelity/PROTOCOL.md:42; all 26 stored applicability records are SKIP with no failure).
evaluation_questions: Q1 (production agreement): How often does the production LLM gate (Gemma, production prompt and budget, each sentence sent as a one-source case) RETRIEVE on sentences the authors labelled positive or negative? Measured as P, R, FPR and fail-closed rate on LADDER test (attack-pattern scheme) and MalwareTextDB test (malware-action scheme). This is agreement with each authors' scheme, not 'applicability accuracy'.

Q2 (fair head-to-head): At the LLM gate's single operating point, does the LLM gate beat an XLM-R classifier that is also cross-scheme on that set, at matched FPR? That is E4 (MTDB-trained) on LADDER and E3 (LADDER-trained) on MTDB.

Q3 (owner's recall priority): Does OR-combining (LLM RETRIEVE or XLM-R >= source-dev threshold A) raise recall, and at what FPR cost? How does that compare with only changing the prompt to lean towards recall (gate_llm.py:52)?
Q4 (prompt arm): Paired with the production prompt, does the recall-leaning line change recall and FPR (McNemar on the same sentences)?

Q5 ('even when paraphrased'): Does the gate RETRIEVE as often on sentences AnnoCTR's authors class as implicit (the technique is described but not named) as on explicit (the technique is named) sentences? This is the only citable way to test the paraphrase claim, and it covers English CTI only.

Q6 (case-level unit): When the gate sees a multi-sentence window rather than one sentence, how often does it RETRIEVE on windows holding at least one author-positive sentence, and what share of those positive sentences end up inside trigger_text (and so in the RAG query, retrieve.py:40)? What does the 4,000-character cut remove?
Q7 (cost and thinking): What does one gate call cost on Gemma, given the 8,192-token thinking budget, and does turning thinking off change any decisions?
Q8 (stability): How often does the decision flip between two identical calls at temperature 0 on the hosted providers?

risks_and_limits: Neither author scheme is 'ATT&CK applicability'. LADDER labels attack patterns; MTDB labels malware actions and leaves human attacker actions as negatives (malwaretextdb_data.py:9-11). Every number is agreement with one scheme. Claims of applicability accuracy, and of any cause for disagreement, are forbidden, as RUN_LOG section 25 already forbids them for RQ1.

Unit mismatch: production judges a whole case, while R1 sends one sentence as a one-source case. Short context-free phrases, such as LADDER's 5-word-or-shorter positives, are harder than in real narratives. R4 windows are only a proxy (window rule is ours), and MTDB has only 8 test reports, so window and report CIs will be wide.
The LLM gate is binary, so it has no AUROC. Comparisons are at its operating point (matched FPR). The 'right' operating point is the owner's value decision, not an empirical result.
Fairness trap: the shipped checkpoint and E3 are in-domain on LADDER. Using them there as competitors would overstate the classifier, so they are reported only as ceilings.

Model drift: the only stored LLM decisions are from deepseek-v4.1-flash at an old budget. They may not be presented as production. Hosted Gemma through nextbit/coreweave may be nondeterministic (R0 flip rate), and pinned providers with allow_fallbacks false can fail as provider errors, which fail closed.

Cost uncertainty: Gemma's gate thinking length has never been observed. The estimates span USD 0.90 to 7.15 for R1, so R0 must come first and its measured per-call mean replaces the proxy. Caps are hard stops.

Paraphrase: the AnnoCTR implicit class is the only citable operationalisation. It covers English CTI, not Thai incident text, so 'even when paraphrased' can be claimed only in that narrow form. AnnoCTR 'none' may contain unlinked behaviour, so FPR there is context, not a result.

Stored-run bookkeeping: results_run2/llm_gate/summary.json says 4,348 calls while the jsonl files hold 4,438 rows. Its spend (USD 1.328) is a key-usage delta, not per-call receipts, so it is not used for Gemma costing.
Multiple comparisons: register at most 5 locked comparisons (as in section 25) before R1. Everything else is descriptive.

citation_checks.note: On arXiv, correctly marked as a preprint. It supports partially: it is a cost-saving cascade that stops at a cheaper model when a scorer judges the answer reliable. Fix 1 stops only on positive answers, which is asymmetric, so describe it as 'in the spirit of' FrugalGPT.

fairness_problems: The 'matched FPR' comparison gives the classifier a threshold chosen on the test labels, so it is an oracle. The LLM gate gets no such tuning. The matched thresholds for E4 on LADDER were 0.080, 0.043 and 0.006, far from threshold A (0.24-0.27), and none of them is deployable. As a comparison of an ROC curve against a single point, 'the LLM point lies below the classifier's ROC' is legitimate. 'LLM is dominated' as a deployment claim is not. Always report a deployable comparison beside it: classifier at A, and classifier at a pre-registered source-dev recall target.

Fix 1 (the OR cascade) is compared only with the LLM alone and the classifier at matched FPR. It is never compared with the cheapest recall-oriented alternative: the classifier alone at a lower threshold, with no LLM call. On the saved LADDER data, that alternative wins. OR(LLM, E4@A) has R 0.689 at FPR 0.376, while E4 alone at the same FPR (oracle) reaches R 0.759. With a deployable threshold, set at 0.90 recall on MTDB dev, E4 alone reaches R 0.687 at mean FPR 0.297. That matches the OR's recall at lower FPR with no LLM cost. The shipped checkpoint alone at the OR's FPR reaches R 0.949, against 0.952 for OR(LLM, shipped@0.1). A reviewer would call fix 1 unmotivated unless Gemma changes this picture.

Running MTDB first, and possibly LADDER not at all under the cap, means the prior-model comparison (deepseek vs Gemma with the same prompt) exists only on LADDER and may never be made. Pre-register which one is primary.

MTDB test has only 8 reports, and one of them (Cylance) holds 212 of the 527 positives (40%). A cluster bootstrap over 8 reports under-covers and is dominated by that report. Report all 8 per-report paired differences and a sign test next to the bootstrap.

The LLM gate sees each sentence alone, without context. The encoder was trained on exactly such sentences, so this unit favours it. RUN_LOG section 15, line 481, shows the LLM accepting short positives at 0.33 with context against 0.16 without. So Q1 and Q2 understate the LLM relative to production, and R4 windows are the fairer unit for the head-to-head.

The trigger-coverage metric (Q6) favours the encoder by construction: it returns whole sentences, up to 16, while the LLM returns sub-spans. Pair coverage with trigger precision and query length, as results_run2/gate_arms/summary.md already does (encoder 923 query characters vs LLM 327).
missing_items: Free analysis F8, to add now: the classifier alone at a pre-registered source-dev recall target (0.90), compared with the LLM and with OR at deployable thresholds, on LADDER (E4, from saved MTDB-dev scores) and later on MTDB (E3, from saved LADDER-dev scores; shipped checkpoint, whose LADDER-dev scores already exist). This is the baseline fix 1 has to beat.

Truncation risk under the current budget: Gemma overshoots its 8,192-token thinking budget (up to 12,879 tokens recorded), so about 1% of gate calls may be cut off at max_tokens 9,216. R1 should log stop_reason and thinking tokens, and fix 5 should be judged on R1, not R0.

Free check of truncation exposure on case-like text: 12 of 103 CASIE analysis-baseline cases exceed 4,000 characters. Where in those cases do sentences describing technique-like behaviour fall? This can be reported descriptively only, since CASIE has no applicability label.
MTDB label-quality limitation: token-level kappa 0.36 and a release/paper count mismatch (RUN_LOG section 24, malwaretextdb_data.py:13-14).
Per-report results for the 8 MTDB test reports, plus a sign test, because one report holds 40% of the positives.
The five locked comparisons, named before R0 (proposal in the corrected plan).
Trigger precision and RAG query length as Q6 metrics next to coverage.
Pretraining contamination as a limitation: LADDER and the 2014 APTnotes reports behind MTDB are public text that both Gemma and XLM-R may have seen.
An explicit statement that all gate evidence is English CTI while production cases are Thai. 'Even when paraphrased' can be claimed only for AnnoCTR's English implicit class.

The 'never' ablation's downstream value (does ATT&CK context help the analysis) needs RAG calls. It stays outside this plan and needs owner approval, as the plan says. It also means no result here shows that the gate's decisions matter for the analysis.

The flip-rate estimate from R0 (60 pairs) is weak: 0 flips gives a 95% upper bound of about 5%. Either report it as a bound, or re-send a 200-item subset of R1 as a pre-registered stability check (about USD 0.29 central).
verdict.corrected_plan_summary:
QUESTIONS. Q1: agreement of the production gate (Gemma, production prompt and budget) with each author scheme, on LADDER test and MTDB test, one sentence per call. Report P, R, FPR, F1 and fail-closed rate, with stop_reason recorded. Q2: the LLM point against cross-scheme XLM-R (E4 on LADDER, E3 on MTDB), reported two ways and labelled as such: (a) whether the LLM point lies above or below the classifier's ROC (oracle matched FPR), and (b) deployable comparisons, with the classifier at A and at a pre-registered source-dev 0.90 recall target. Q3: recall options for the owner's priority, all compared at deployable thresholds: OR cascade, classifier alone at the lower dev threshold, and the line-52 prompt ablation. Q4: line-52 ablation paired with production (McNemar). Q5: RETRIEVE rate per AnnoCTR author class (implicit, explicit, both, with none as context); English CTI only. Q6: 5-sentence MTDB windows: P, R, FPR, trigger coverage, trigger precision, query length. Q7: cost and thinking-off. Q8: flip rate reported as a bound.

BASELINES. never; always-RETRIEVE (F1 0.667 on LADDER, 0.447 on MTDB); TF-IDF E1/E2 at A; XLM-R E3/E4 (3 seeds) at A, at a dev recall target and at oracle matched FPR (labelled ROC comparison); the shipped checkpoint at 0.1 (production), at its saved LADDER-dev max-F1 0.594 and at a dev 0.90 recall target, in-domain on LADDER and so reported there only as a ceiling; the earlier LLM model (deepseek, identical prompt, effective max_tokens 1,024) as a prior-model reference.

METRICS. All judge-free. Fail-closed counts as SKIP everywhere, including the exploratory AnnoCTR rates (0.740 / 0.529 / 0.825 / 0.223). Paired bootstrap, 2,000 resamples, over reports for MTDB (plus per-report differences and a sign test) and over sentences for LADDER (limitation stated). McNemar (Dror 2018). Flip rate (Atil 2025). Provider-reported USD per call.

LOCKED COMPARISONS (at most 5, pre-registered): (1) Gemma LLM vs E3 on MTDB at A and at the dev recall target; (2) Gemma LLM vs E4 on LADDER, same; (3) OR(LLM, classifier@A) vs classifier alone at the dev recall target, on MTDB; (4) line-52 ablation vs production, McNemar on MTDB; (5) Gemma vs deepseek on LADDER with the identical prompt. Everything else is descriptive.

FREE ANALYSES. F1: stored LADDER head-to-head, saved as a script; the numbers reproduce exactly (LLM tp 206, fp 114, fn 125, tn 217; E4 matched R 0.680/0.758/0.776; OR +0.066 R, +0.031 FPR). F2: shipped checkpoint on MTDB dev and test, CPU only; LADDER dev is already scored. F3: truncation, on MTDB as one source (467/527) and on CASIE case lengths (12/103 over 4,000). F4: windows and sensitivity at sizes 3/5/8 (612/370/232 windows). F5: cascade call saving (E4 fires on 35-40% of LADDER). F6: exploratory AnnoCTR rates. F7: cost model refit on 260 receipts (CoreWeave 0.1003/0.3029, NextBit 0.0892/0.2996 USD/M). F8 (new): the classifier-alone recall-target baseline. On the stored model it already matches OR at lower FPR (E4 dev-0.90: R 0.687, FPR 0.297; OR: R 0.689, FPR 0.376).

PAID RUNS, none needing RAG. Per call: USD 0.00145 on the preflight proxy (upper-leaning), 0.000629 on the prose proxy, 0.00287 at the max_tokens ceiling. R0 pilot, 120 calls: 0.174 central, cap 0.35. R1, 2,493 calls: 3.62 central (1.57 prose proxy, 7.16 worst). The cap must be at least R0-rate x 1,831 x 1.2 so that MTDB completes (worst case 5.26 for MTDB alone), or MTDB is subsampled by report as pre-registered. R4 windows, 370 calls: 0.55, cap 1.1. Optional: R2 line-52 ablation 3.62 (cap 4); R3 thinking-off 0.31 (cap 1.05; Gemma is known to honour disabled thinking); R5 AnnoCTR 1.55 (cap 1.6). Core total 4.34 central (caps 5.45 plus the R1 cap revision); all runs 9.80 central, 12.10 in caps. RAG downstream effect: not planned, needs owner approval.

FIXES, all proposals needing owner approval. (1) Recall option: adopt the OR cascade only if it beats the classifier alone at a dev recall target on MTDB (comparison 3); otherwise the cheaper fix is lowering the encoder threshold. Cite SuperICL only for 'small models complement LLMs', and FrugalGPT (PREPRINT) for the cost cascade. (2) Line-52 prompt change, only if R2 shows a recall gain without an FPR cost larger than fix 1's. (3) Replace shadow threshold 0.1 with a LADDER-dev-derived one (0.594 max-F1 is saved; a 0.90 recall target is to be computed), with MTDB results from F2. (4) Thinking off for the gate, if R3's McNemar shows no decision change. (5) Output budget: judge from R1's stop_reason. About 1% truncation is expected from Gemma overshooting its thinking budget, so raising max_tokens or turning thinking off (fix 4) may be needed.

LIMITS. The results measure agreement with each author scheme, not 'applicability accuracy'. Every call sees one context-free sentence, which understates the LLM. MTDB has 8 reports, one with 40% of the positives, and token-level kappa 0.36. All evidence is English CTI while production is Thai. Pretraining contamination is possible. The eval46 threshold and the '100% LLM gate' result may not be cited.

plan.component: 3. Reading: the first model call of the analysis, which writes claims with exact quotations, plus parties, timeline and impacts
plan.what_it_does:
Verified in code, read-only.
- write_trace (backend/app/analysis/write.py:15-42) makes two calls in sequence. The first is the reading: request_stage with stage "case_reading", CASE_READING_SYSTEM_PROMPT and schema CaseProviderReading (write.py:24-30). The second is the judgement (write.py:32-41). joined_trace (write.py:103-120) takes claims, involved_parties, timeline and impacts from the reading, and summary, gaps and mitre_associations from the judgement.
- The reading is not shown MITRE context. reading_request (write.py:45-54) sends only response_language, case_sources and followup_history. technical_context is added only in write_request, which feeds the judgement (write.py:57-73). The prompt says the same thing (backend/app/analysis/prompts.py:154-156).
- The reading schema is CaseProviderReading (backend/app/trace/trace.py:137-144): version, claims (at most 64), involved_parties, timeline and impacts, with extra="forbid".
  - A party is name plus a free-text role plus claim_ids (trace.py:20-33). The role has no fixed vocabulary, so there is no victim/attacker field.
  - A timeline item is a free-text time plus event plus claim_ids (trace.py:36-49). An impact is description plus claim_ids (trace.py:52-64).
- A claim (backend/app/trace/claims.py:115-123, 179-182) has claim_id, claim_type, text, epistemic_status, source ids, citations and reasoning_summary.
  - claim_type is reported, analytical_inference or unknown (claims.py:15).
  - epistemic_status has six values: reported, suspected, contradicted, not_established, unknown, not_confirmed (claims.py:18-25).
- The prompt (prompts.py:145-193) says only "Distinguish reported facts, qualified analytical inferences, and unknowns" (prompts.py:169). It never defines the six statuses. In backend/app, "suspected" appears only in claims.py:20 and in the report label table (backend/app/reports/display.py:34).
- After the reading, the binder (backend/app/trace/bind.py) acts on it:
  - resolve_claim keeps only citations whose quote is located in the named source (bind.py:191-214, 254-281).
  - confirmed_status changes only "reported" with no surviving supporting citation to "not_confirmed" (bind.py:217-220). No other status is checked.
  - Party, timeline and impact claim_ids are filtered to existing claims (bind.py:99-102).
- How statuses are shown to the reader:
  - Report labels: reported = "appears in the source", suspected = "under investigation", unknown = "not known" (display.py:32-39).
  - The frontend has a "Suspected" section in the analysis overview (frontend/src/features/analysis/overview.ts:37).
evaluation_questions: Q1 (done, needs B2): does a separate reading call state and ground more of CASIE's annotated main-event facts than one structured call and than prose, and does the gain come from the extra call or from field order (summary last)?
Q2: of the main-event facts production misses, which roles are they and where are they lost: never written by the reading, or written and then dropped by the binder?
Q3: when the source hedges, negates or projects an event (CASIE realis Other), does the claim text keep the hedge or negation, or does a suspicion become a stated fact?

Q4: does epistemic_status tell hedged claims from factual ones better than the trivial labeller that marks everything 'reported'? Does it collapse (a whole trace marked 'unknown'), and is it consistent with claim_type?
Q5: are general or background statements (CASIE realis Generic) presented as this case's timeline events or impacts?
Q6 (descriptive only): are victims and attackers ever given each other's role? This cannot be scored without a mapping of our own.
Q7: how stable is the reading from run to run? One run per case, so not measured yet.
Q8: can a definition of the statuses in the reading prompt, or a deterministic cue rule, make the status informative without losing recall?

metrics.name: Main-event recall, frozen V0 (primary for Q1)
metrics.definition: Gold main-event facts stated in the arm's own text / gold main-event facts. Whole-token match after normalisation, quotations excluded, a failed run scores 0. Reported with V1, V3 and V6 and the matched-length control
metrics.precedent: Wiseman, Shieber and Rush, EMNLP 2017, doi:10.18653/v1/D17-1239 (content selection); Simonsohn et al. 2020, doi:10.1038/s41562-020-0912-z; Sun, Shapira et al. 2019, doi:10.18653/v1/W19-2303

metrics.name: Reading-field recall
metrics.definition: The same V0 recall over the reading's fields only (parties, timeline, claims, impacts), leaving out the judgement's summary and gaps. Attributes the recall to the component under test
metrics.precedent: FActScore (Min et al., EMNLP 2023, doi:10.18653/v1/2023.emnlp-main.741): scoring per atomic unit rather than the whole text

metrics.name: Per-step loss table
metrics.definition: Each gold main-event fact falls in exactly one class: stated; quoted but not stated; in a written quotation but dropped or placed elsewhere by the binder; never written. Broken down by CASIE role
metrics.precedent: LADDER per-step false negatives (Alam et al. 2023, doi:10.1145/3607199.3607208)

metrics.name: Verbatim rate
metrics.definition: Quotations located by the binder / quotations written (grounding report)
metrics.precedent: Zhang et al., Verifiable by Construction, preprint arXiv:2609.15964 (stage 2)

metrics.name: Hedge and negation preservation (Q3)
metrics.definition: Over claims whose verified supporting quotation overlaps only realis-Other attack nuggets and contains a cue of class k (negation, modal, future): the share whose claim text contains a cue of the same class. The lexicon is frozen before scoring the test cases. Reported per class, with a strict and a broad lexicon as the sensitivity check
metrics.precedent: NegEx trigger lists (Chapman et al., J Biomed Inform 2001, doi:10.1006/jbin.2001.1029); BioScope cue classes (Vincze et al., BMC Bioinformatics 2008, doi:10.1186/1471-2105-9-S11-S9); realis in Rich ERE (Song et al. 2015, doi:10.3115/v1/W15-0812)

metrics.name: Status discrimination (Q4)
metrics.definition: The share of non-'reported' statuses on Other+modal claims minus the share on Actual-only claims, with a case bootstrap. Also the full status x realis contingency table and Cramer's V. Must exceed 0, which the all-'reported' labeller scores
metrics.precedent: Event factuality values (Sauri and Pustejovsky, FactBank, LRE 2009, doi:10.1007/s10579-009-9089-9); Murzaku and Rambow, CODI 2025, doi:10.18653/v1/2025.codi-1.10

metrics.name: Status collapse rate
metrics.definition: The share of traces in which every claim is 'unknown' while at least one claim's verified quotation overlaps an Actual nugget. Also the share of analytical_inference claims with status 'reported'
metrics.precedent: ours (a consistency count); reported as a deviation, not a headline

metrics.name: Generic-as-case-event count
metrics.definition: Claims whose verified quotations overlap only Generic-realis nuggets and that are referenced by a timeline item or an impact, per run
metrics.precedent: The Generic realis class in Rich ERE (Song et al. 2015)

metrics.name: Stability
metrics.definition: Mean pairwise Jaccard of the stated main-event fact sets over runs of the same case
metrics.precedent: Relins et al. 2025, doi:10.1007/s10940-025-09611-z (repeated-prompt variability); the frozen README metric

metrics.name: Cost, time and completion per case
metrics.definition: Provider-reported USD per call, model time p50/p90/max, and the completion rate. The primary recall figure is the completion rate times the mean completed score

risks_and_limits: B2 is running in the shared checkout at this moment (results file written at 07:43). Do not start another harness in that checkout until it ends: read its summary JSON, and work in your own worktree (owner memory: shared checkout).

All the realis and cue figures here are exploratory, computed before any pre-registration, on cases 1-50 that have now been inspected. They can motivate the study but cannot be its evidence. Only cases 51-100 with a frozen protocol count.

CASIE realis is event-level and Other is a mix: modal 313, negation 262, future 56, no cue 99 of 562 Other attack events. 'Other' is not 'suspected'. Any realis-to-status mapping is ours and must be stated as such, with a strict and a broad variant.
A claim can be hedged in its text and still be correctly 'reported' (the source reports a hedge). Status discrimination must be read alongside text-level cue preservation, not alone.
Small numbers: 43 Other-only production claims in cases 1-50 and 44 Other attack events in cases 51-100. Status-level differences below about 0.15 will not be detectable. Recall's MDE is about 0.11.
CASIE gold contains noise: a negated argument inside an Actual event (135 'financial data'), background incidents marked Actual, and about 3.5% of offsets off by one character.
Time confound: arms run on different days on hosted models (Atil et al. 2025). Same-batch controls are proposed for the status study; for B2 a same-time single rerun is optional.
The articles are 2017-2019 news that the model may have seen. Whole-token matching favours text close to the source's wording (production is the most extractive: density 4.24).

The cost estimates assume the same model (google/gemma-4-26b-a4b-it) and provider order (coreweave/bf16, nextbit/bf16) as recorded. Provider speed and runaway rate vary by hour, and a runaway call costs the most.
Any prompt or binder change is a production change and needs the owner's approval. It would also change RQ2's inputs, so RQ2 hashes and figures stay tied to the old commit.

datasets.our_rules: Main-event definition; the key-to-role mapping, with 'present' meaning a role fact exists in any Actual attack event. Both already pre-registered in their READMEs, and both must be marked as ours. A number-derivation rule (rounding, time arithmetic), if used, must be fixed before scoring; otherwise report derivations separately as 'not verbatim'. Sensitivity: the four keys against the three keys against all seven, and the main event against all events (free).

datasets.name: AnnoCTR test split (34 documents), for the optional ATT&CK run only
datasets.citation: Lange et al., LREC-COLING 2024, doi:10.63317/4esp6coivous; arXiv:2404.07765 (experiments/gate_generalization/citation_verification.md:10)
datasets.labels_used: Author technique links (linking_mitre_only, attack.mitre.org/techniques), taken as each document's set of linked technique IDs.
datasets.our_rules: Taking the union of mention-level links as the document gold is our aggregation. The oracle mitre_table (gold techniques plus k distractors sampled from the local STIX bundle with a fixed seed) is our construction and must be pre-registered. Sensitivity: k in {5, 10}, and explicit-only against all links.

metrics.name: Summary identifier support
metrics.definition: Of the dates, numbers of two or more digits, URLs, IPs, hashes, ATT&CK IDs and domains in the summary (harness regexes, trace IDs removed), the share found (a) in the article and (b) in the reading's claim text plus kept quotes. Derivations are reported separately.
metrics.precedent: Wiseman, Shieber and Rush EMNLP 2017, record-level precision, doi:10.18653/v1/D17-1239; RQ2's new-identifier count

metrics.name: Summary entity precision against the source and against the reading
metrics.definition: Share of named entities in the summary whose normalised string occurs in the source, and in the reading. Needs a local NER (spaCy is not installed). The capitalised-span regex tried during planning is too noisy to report (it flags 'because' and 'during').
metrics.precedent: Nan et al., Entity-level Factual Consistency of Abstractive Text Summarization, EACL 2021, pp. 2727-2733, doi:10.18653/v1/2021.eacl-main.235 (verified on Crossref)

metrics.name: Summary-only facts
metrics.definition: Gold facts stated in the summary but in no reading field. This measures whether the summary rests on the claims.
metrics.precedent: Attribute First (Slobodkin et al. ACL 2024, doi:10.18653/v1/2024.acl-long.182) as the design precedent: generate from selected content. ALCE (doi:10.18653/v1/2023.emnlp-main.398) citation recall is the entailment-based analogue; ours is string-based.

metrics.name: Summary main-event recall, full and matched length
metrics.definition: Gold main-event facts stated in the summary ÷ gold main-event facts, frozen whole-token scorer; longer summary truncated to the shorter one's word count; V1 and V3 scorer variants.
metrics.precedent: Wiseman et al. 2017 content selection; AGIR fact recall (doi:10.1109/BigData59044.2023.10386116); Sun, Shapira et al. 2019 matched length (doi:10.18653/v1/W19-2303)

metrics.name: Gap-key agreement
metrics.definition: Per case, the Jaccard of checklist gap-key sets and of eligible-gap key sets: judgement against preflight, against judgement against judgement and preflight against preflight. Also the share of cases where the judgement has an eligible gap and the preflight had none.
metrics.precedent: Pairwise-Jaccard stability, as used in README:121 (Relins et al., doi:10.1007/s10940-025-09611-z)

metrics.name: Gap listing rate on CASIE-present and CASIE-absent keys
metrics.definition: Share of keys with CASIE-annotated facts that get a gap (a false-alarm proxy), against keys with none. Three-key primary; four and seven keys as sensitivity.
metrics.precedent: Chaparro et al. ESEC/FSE 2017, missing-information detection with precision and recall, doi:10.1145/3106237.3106285

metrics.name: Reference integrity counts
metrics.definition: Gap claim references dropped, trace IDs in the summary, associations_outside_context, associations_without_claim, schema rejections, runaways.
metrics.precedent: ALCE-style automatic citation-quality counts (doi:10.18653/v1/2023.emnlp-main.398)

metrics.name: Association precision and recall against author technique labels (optional run)
metrics.definition: Document-level technique IDs linked by the judgement against the AnnoCTR author set, with oracle context; the trivial baselines as bounds.
metrics.precedent: TTP-extraction evaluation by technique-set precision and recall: SoK, Büchel et al. USENIX Security 2025, pp. 4621-4641 (verified table in related_studies_modules.md)

risks_and_limits: The planning-time figures (summary support, the −0.073 summary recall, gap-key rates) were computed on data I had already looked at. They are exploratory; F1 to F3 must be frozen in the README before they are run as the reported analysis, and described as post hoc.
One run per case in the main run. Summary and gap metrics from a single run mix arm effects with run-to-run noise, which is why R1 and R2 each include self-agreement.

The saved traces predate the gap 'topic' prompt line (prompts.py:27-28, ec50f9c). R1 uses the current prompt, so it cannot be compared cleanly with the saved judgement outputs. Compare R1 against itself for stability, and against the saved runs only descriptively.
Judgement-only reruns hold the reading fixed, so they leave out reading variance. Case 132 shows a degenerate reading can drive judgement errors.

CASIE is 2017-2019 English news: short, rarely in conflict, possibly in the model's training data, and without ATT&CK labels. Nothing here carries over to Thai cases, and the Thai dataset is excluded.
Summary identifier counts are small (88 items over 48 summaries), and exact regexes miss spelled-out numbers ('five'). Ceiling effects make a between-arm difference unlikely to be detectable.
'Absent' in CASIE means 'not annotated as an attack-event argument', not 'not in the article', so the gap-key rates are a proxy under our rule. who_responsible gold is unreliable (audit §2).
The ATT&CK results depend on the other student's retrieval (R6). The oracle run (R5) measures linking only, under ideal context, and its distractor rule is ours.
Hosted providers are not deterministic (Atil et al. Eval4NLP 2025, doi:10.18653/v1/2025.eval4nlp-1.12). Runs made at different times confound time with arm (README:419-421).

QUESTIONS.
- Q1: Are the judgement's free-text fields supported? That means the summary and also the gap description, reason and question, at identifier level (primary) and entity level (secondary, only after a local NER is approved).
- Q2: Does the separate judgement call matter? First, report the pre-registered B2 primary. Then ask, post hoc, whether the judgement summary covers fewer main-event facts than the one-call summaries at matched length.
- Q3: How far do judgement gap keys agree with preflight gap keys on the same input, measured against each component's own run-to-run ceiling? It is descriptive. The 'unasked eligible gap' check is restricted to cases where the preflight finds no eligible gap, because Proceed also happens by design after max_rounds or gaps_exhausted (clarification.py:44-66).
- Q4: Gap listing rate on CASIE-present versus absent keys. Primary: four one-to-one keys (who_affected, who_responsible, when, where; audit line 43). Sensitivity: three keys without who_responsible, and all seven; any status and NOT_PROVIDED-only; main event and all events. All of these are our rules and are pre-registered.
- Q5: Conflicts, descriptive only; correctness cannot be measured on CASIE.
- Q6: ATT&CK linking, optional and approval-gated.
- Q7: Integrity: dangling gap references (28 in case 132), unresolved summary IDs, version-literal rejections, runaways, and cost.

BASELINES.
- single and single_late (saved; time confound for single_late).
- Preflight (R2) and the noise ceilings (R1/R2 self-agreement).
- Trivial gap baselines: list nothing, list all keys.
- For R5 only: empty list and link-everything.
- R3 is compared against R1 from the same batch, not against the saved arms.

METRICS. All judge-free:
- identifier support against the article and the reading (Wiseman 2017), with derivations reported separately;
- entity precision against the source (Nan et al. 2021, doi:10.18653/v1/2021.eacl-main.235), once NER is approved;
- summary-only facts;
- summary main-event recall with the frozen scorer, at full and matched length (Sun, Shapira et al. 2019), V1 and V3;
- gap-key Jaccard (the Relins precedent is inherited and its support unverified);
- listing rates (Chaparro 2017);
- integrity counts, with no literature claimed (ALCE is only the entailment analogue);
- association precision and recall (SoK 2025).

FREE ANALYSES (freeze the scripts and hashes in the README first).
- F0: run b2_analysis.py and write the B2 result section. single_late − single +0.021 [−0.043, +0.083], p 0.547. cybercase − single_late +0.091 [+0.004, +0.182], p 0.047, Holm 0.094. Matched length −0.010. Report completed-only too.

- F2: summary recall with robustness.py/bootstrap.py, sign-flip with Holm, matched length, V1 and V3.
- F3: listing rates with the four-key primary.
- F4: an instrumented re-bind in research/ that counts dropped gap references, unresolved summary IDs and unsupported identifiers.
- F5: conflict table.
- F6: per-stage cost and runaways.
- F7: NER entity precision, after download approval.

PAID RUNS (research harness only, gate never, no RAG).
- Core R1: judgement-only reruns, 2 × 48 on the saved written readings with the current production prompt; also count schema rejections. 96 × 0.001931 = USD 0.185, cap 0.25.
- Core R2: preflight, 2 × 48 on full text, current prompt. Length-adjusted from recorded assess costs: USD 0.141 (0.137 unadjusted), cap 0.20.
- Core total about USD 0.33, cap 0.45.
- Optional R3: element-aware summary, 48 calls, run in the same batch as R1. Only if F2's matched-length deficit survives. USD 0.091, cap 0.15.
- Optional R4: judgement without sources, USD 0.091. Low value.
- Optional R5: AnnoCTR test 34 documents with an oracle table (gold plus seeded STIX distractors, k in {5, 10}, pre-registered). Needs owner approval. Length-scaled estimate USD 0.335: smoke 3 documents with a 0.05 cap, then main cap 0.50.
- R6: real gate plus RAG. Needs owner approval, is the other student's scope, and has no recorded cost basis, so it is kept separate.

FIXES (all production, all need owner approval).
- (1) Add count-only counters to CaseGroundingReport for dropped gap claim references, unresolved summary/gap IDs, and summary or gap identifiers found in neither claims nor quotes. Check with F4: 28 references in 1 case, 0 unresolved IDs, 0 unsupported identifiers, and no other change to the trace.
- (2) Drop the ID-stripping fix: IDs are valid references and the prompt does not forbid them.
- (3) An element-aware summary instruction (SumCoT; Narayan (*)), only if R3 beats R1 at matched length without losing identifier support.
- (4) Share the preflight keys with the judgement only if cross-agreement falls below both ceilings on the no_eligible_gap subset. It is an engineering choice with no literature claim, and its rerun costs USD 0.091.

risks_and_limits: The edge quote-mark rule was derived from the same 9 main-run failures it fixes. In-sample recovery (4/4) is not evidence. Only the RQ2 outputs (0 wrappers), the mutation set and optional new cases are out of sample, and the event is rare (about 0.5% of quotations), so even 50 new cases give only about 4 events.
Mutation expectations are ours. 'Join two words' and 'lower-case first letter' have debatable correct outcomes and must be reported as such, not as errors.

Verbatim is not support. The binder checks string presence only, and the negation and hedge heuristics have unknown precision because no annotation is allowed. Casual inspection suggests most of the 25 candidates are benign ('false identities', 'in no time'), but that is not a label.
CASIE is 2017-2019 English news. Frequencies do not transfer to Thai case files, OCR text or complaints. Thai risks (ZWSP, PUA, digits) are unit behaviour only.
No ATT&CK association has ever been checked on a citable output. That check stays unmeasured unless the owner approves a RAG run.
The status-rule effect is dominated by the writer model's quoting habit (1.1% vs 36.2%), so binder numbers must be reported per model and not pooled.
The 'paraphrased' count in the grounding report includes verbatim quotes with wrappers, so it overstates paraphrasing until the fix lands.
The B2 (single_late) jsonl was still growing when read (49 rows, USD 0.12836, last write 07:40 on 2026-09-30). The brief's '15/50, USD 0.0397' is stale, and single_late numbers here are provisional.

critique.strongest_fix_with_literature:
The strongest single fix is explicit status definitions in the preflight gap prompt. It separates NOT_PROVIDED (the text states no fact for the key) from AMBIGUOUS (a fact is stated, but vaguely). It would be tested first as the research-only definitions-only arm, at USD 0.285 (200 × 0.0014230 per call, provider-reported in detect_main_20260928_075016.jsonl).

The measured problem is the clearest of any component:
- The system asks with P 0.54 and R 0.42, against 0.31 / 0.30 for the same-budget checklist.
- 28 of its 34 false positives are requests for more specific information about facts the text already states ('hackers' → which group, 'today' → which date), labelled NOT_PROVIDED.
- On the visible text, 58 of 69 keys whose fact is present are still marked NOT_PROVIDED.
- The cause is visible in the code: the production prompt lists the four status names and defines none of them (backend/app/analysis/prompts.py:34).

The literature is verified and fits:
- AmbigQA (Min et al., EMNLP 2020, doi:10.18653/v1/2020.emnlp-main.466) and CLAMBER (ACL 2024, doi:10.18653/v1/2024.acl-long.578) separate an underspecified answer from a missing one. Both were checked on Crossref.
- Chaparro et al. (ESEC/FSE 2017, doi:10.1145/3106237.3106285) supports scoring missing-element detection by precision and recall.
- MediQ (NeurIPS 2024, doi:10.52202/079017-0908) supports the withholding design.

Honest limits:
- The status definitions and the rule that a specificity request on a present fact counts as a false positive are ours. They have to be pre-registered and scored under a strict and a lenient 'present' rule.
- The fix does not address the null withholding effect. That is B1's job.
- It is English CASIE only.

It beats the alternatives on the quality of its evidence:
- The edge quote-mark binder fix has a precisely measured cause, but 4 of 869 (0.46%) is a tiny effect, derived in-sample, and its literature fit is weak.
- The gate recall fixes rest on the earlier deepseek model; nothing has been measured on Gemma.
- The reading status definitions have a clear symptom (0 of 848 claims 'suspected'), but only framing literature: Murzaku and Rambow 2025 shows the task is hard.
critique.honest_bottom_line:
What can be claimed now, all from saved files at no cost:

(1) Reading plus judgement beats one structured call on CASIE main-event recall: 0.779 against 0.667, +0.112 BCa [+0.038, +0.195]. The gain survives scorer variants and is not explained by length. The pre-registered B2 test says the gain comes from the split, not from field order: single_late − single is +0.021 [−0.043, +0.083], and on the 47 completed cases single_late is actually below single. The split's own margin over single_late is borderline (+0.091, Holm p 0.094). The gain sits in the detail fields the reading writes, not in the judgement's summary or gaps.

(2) Follow-up asking is more precise than a same-budget checklist that does not read the case: P 0.54 against 0.31, robust with Holm p 0.0002. But withholding a sentence does not change what it asks (McNemar p=1.0). The claim therefore has to be 'better targeted questions', not 'asks about what is missing'. Most false positives are specificity requests, which count as errors only under our own status definition.

(3) The binder locates 860 of 869 quotations. At most 4 of the 9 rejections were wrong (0.46%). It demotes unverified 'reported' claims as designed. Verbatim is not support, and a collapsed trace (case 132) reports as perfect.

What cannot be claimed yet:
- Anything about the production Gemma gate on citable data. The only LLM-gate numbers on LADDER come from the earlier deepseek model, so component 2's baseline needs the paid R0/R1 (about USD 4.3), unless the owner approves a cheaper LADDER-only run.
- That ATT&CK context improves the analysis. That needs RAG and is outside our scope.
- That an answered follow-up improves the analysis. Not measured by any plan; it needs the new injection test.
- That epistemic statuses carry information (0 of 848 claims 'suspected'; status definitions are absent).
- Anything about Thai cases.
- 'Even when paraphrased' for the gate, beyond an exploratory English AnnoCTR implicit-class rate of 0.740.

The whole core programme costs about USD 6.55 central, or 2.21 without the gate, and the full set about USD 14.03. That is small money. The real constraints are the owner's decisions on the gate cap, the harness changes and RAG, plus doing the free, pre-registration steps first, so that none of the new numbers is post hoc.
